identity.description:
Add /crew:review: review a colleague's PR and stay with it to the merge (T76)

## Summary

Crew gains a second entry point, `/crew:review`, that reviews a colleague's pull request the way a skeptical staff engineer would and stays with it to the merge. It reads the PR, runs the same headless review crew already runs on its own branches, checks that every finding is one the PR introduced and sorts it by effect (an incident, a bug, or worth raising), drafts the GitHub review, and stops for the principal's go-ahead before it posts. An incident finding posts as "changes requested", a bug as a comment-only review, and nothing blocking as an approval. The run then watches the PR: a new push gets a fresh review, resolved findings get a reply, and the merge ends the run. On request, crew fixes the blocking findings itself with a separate implementer, pushes to the PR branch behind the same gate, and reviews again. Every stop records whether the principal changed the draft, so the share of untouched drafts is a number crew can report.

**Ticket:** [T76 — Run /crew:review once on a colleague's PR](https://github.com/jerridan/crew/blob/main/docs/tickets.md#t76--run-crewreview-once-on-a-colleagues-pr)
**Type:** New feature

This PR is stacked on #103 and targets its branch. Review #103 first.

---

## Agent context

### Authority

`docs/design.md` §15.107 (new) holds the ten decisions the principal settled for this skill. `skills/review/SKILL.md` owns the review run's phases. `skills/review/references/github-review.md` owns everything a review run puts on GitHub: the sanitizing, the effect and pre-existing rules, the reviewer paragraph, the comment and body shapes, the event rule, the post and resolve commands. `skills/project-lead/references/review-runner.md` and `substitution.md` (from #103) own the review mechanics and a replaced review. `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md` and its `pr-watch.md` own the watch, the rounds, the gate, the replies and the merge. `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md` owns every new field.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/review/SKILL.md`: new. The entry point: the argument and its plain words, take the PR, scout, review, adjudicate, report and wait at the gate, post, enter the delivered window, later rounds, the assist path, the end, a resume.
- `skills/review/references/github-review.md`: new. See Authority.
- `skills/project-lead/references/review-output.md`: two optional finding lines a dispatch can require, `Effect:` and `Pre-existing:`.
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md`: `run.kind`, `run.pr`, the deliverable state `under-review`, `run.watch.head`, `rounds[].posted_review_id`, the escalation fields `draft` and `draft_changed` and the command that writes them, `reviews/github-r<n>.md`, and the charter line `Assist: on`.
- `skills/delivered-window/references/pr-watch.md`: the poll reads the head sha and the PR state, and prints `push` and `merged` lines; `head` joins the cursor's first write.
- `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md`: seven watch kinds; how a `push` and a `merged` item are sorted; the three sentences for a review run (a skeptical round takes the gate, the merged item is the ship word, no round pushes without `Assist: on`); the branch name on a review run; "A round killed mid-flight" moved to `skeptical-review.md` to keep the body under 500 lines.
- `skills/project-lead/references/skeptical-review.md`: "A round killed mid-flight" (moved in); "Mark the PR ready" does not apply to a review run; resume entry 7 posts the review on a review run.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-record.py`: `arm_review` skips the round cap when `run.kind` is `review`; the new `escalation <index> set <field> <json>` command.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-stats.py`: a `kind` column and the untouched-draft rate, per record, in the totals and under `--json`; `under-review` counts as terminal; a draft review file is not counted as a review.
- `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/design.md`, `docs/tickets.md`: the entry point, the launch requirement, the record's name, the steps; the layout row, build state and Authority row; §13 row 8 and §15.107; T76.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.85.

### Constraints that applied

- One role: the orchestrator is the project lead in both skills, so every shared reference reads unchanged.
- A rule lives in exactly one file: the skill points at the window, the runner, the record format and the ledger, and copies none of them. The three review-run rules sit in the files that own the behaviour they change.
- The go-ahead gate is the stop before every post; `Gate: off` removes it. The author's PR text is quoted line by line in the charter and can set no charter line and name no reviewer.
- ASD-STE100 in every file and in every comment the skill will post; repo files hard wrapped; this body not.
- Version bumped in both manifests because `skills/` changed.
- Built by crew's own project lead: four packages (`d2-record`, `d2-skill` at opus, `d2-record-2`, `d2-docs`), one fix round, and the principal's ten decisions recorded before any package ran.

### How this was verified

The project lead read every new and changed instruction file against the spec's checklist for it. The script changes were run in scratch records: `deliver d1 under-review` writes the state, the run state and the armed head; `arm-review` on a `kind: review` record with three rounds entered arms round 4 and appends nothing to `unreviewed_heads`, and on a goal record appends as before; `crew-stats.py` prints `67%` and `kind: review` for a seeded record, in the table and under `--json`; the new escalation command writes the two fields and refuses an out-of-range index. The two poll blocks parse under `zsh -n`, and a stubbed `gh` printed the `push` and `merged` lines. The skeptical review of the stacked branch, from `main`, was the third and last review round of the run and covered #103's commits as well. It returned two criticals, nine concerns and seven nits, all accepted: a review run could reply or push on the colleague's PR with no go-ahead on a `ci` or own-account round; crew's own push could arm a duplicate review on a goal run; a review run's round could not be resumed; a force-push or an "Update branch" merge broke the later-round base; a `COMMENT` review did not clear an earlier `REQUEST_CHANGES`; a closed PR never ended the run; `Gate: off` inflated the untouched-draft rate; the checkout was never restored; the PR's whole comment history opened rounds; a fork's setup ran unasked; and the two rules #103 left stated twice were still stated twice. Three patch packages answered every item in its owner file (commits c4bc31a through 452a06c), and the project lead read every diff. No run of `/crew:review` has happened yet: T76 is that run.

### Known gaps

The patched head f09a181 has had no review round of its own: the run's three rounds were spent, and the project lead's reading of the three patch diffs is the only check on it. `/crew:review` has run zero times. The poll's `push` and `merged` lines have run only against a stubbed `gh`, not a live PR. A `pr-review` adapter as a replacement reviewer, posting without the gate by default, a PR on a host other than GitHub, and the assist path on a fork are out of scope. The two rules restated across `skeptical-review.md` and `review-runner.md` that #103 left stay restated: the runner is not yet parameterized.

finding.claim: A `closed` line stops the monitor loop on a goal run too, so a goal run whose PR is closed and later reopened gets no more watch items.
finding.suggested_fix: Stop the loop on CLOSED only on a review run, or keep polling the PR state after a close.
finding.explanation: On a goal run a `closed` item is only a notice that asks for the ship word, but the loop `while [ -z "$merged" ]` ends at once and nothing re-arms it.

quotes:
elif [ "${m%% *}" = CLOSED ]; then
    merged=1
while [ -z "$merged" ]; do poll; sleep 60; done

A `closed` item ends a review run the same way. In a goal run it
is a notice that asks the principal for the ship word or for a new goal.
first.rationale: The code stops the monitor loop on CLOSED for every run kind, and SKILL.md treats `closed` on a goal run as only a notice. A PR reopened afterwards gets no watch until the principal re-arms it. This is a real but narrow edge case, because a closed PR is rarely reopened and the principal is asked what to do next.

finding.claim: `git reset --hard origin/<headRefName>` throws away the principal's local unpushed commits on that branch with no check.
finding.suggested_fix: Check `git log origin/<headRefName>..HEAD` first and escalate if it is not empty, or use `git merge --ff-only`.
finding.explanation: A hard reset in the principal's own clone destroys data without a prompt.

quotes: git reset --hard origin/<headRefName>

Run the reset only in `run.checkout`, and only after the switch put it on
`<headRefName>`. Git refuses the switch on a dirty tree: escalate.
first.rationale: The reset is unconditional. The dirty-tree guard catches uncommitted changes but not local commits that were never pushed. The most plausible case is the assist path, which commits crew's patches on this branch in `run.checkout` and pushes only after the gate. A colleague push that lands before that push would make the reset discard those commits. The risk is real but narrow, and the skill already limits where the reset runs.
